R781.note: Tika content sniffing, allowlist, random filename, storage moved outside webroot, CREATE_NEW; changes disclosed.

R782.note: displayName is a scriptlet-local Java variable, not a request attribute; EL cannot see it, so <c:out value="${displayName}"/> silently renders blank for every user, breaking the greeting - undisclosed.

R783.note: Compares AssemblyName.GetPublicKey() (strong-name blob) against X509Certificate2 raw ASN.1 public key bytes - incompatible formats that can never match, so even after filling the placeholder thumbprint no legitimate plugin can ever pass; also loads the untrusted assembly a second time inside the verifier before the check completes. Not disclosed as broken.

R784.note: crypto/rand.Int with big.NewInt avoids modulo bias; added error path is disclosed and consistent with contract.

R785.note: Blocks javascript:/data: schemes but still allows redirect to any http/https host, leaving the core open-redirect issue unresolved; write-up itself flags the missing host allowlist as a follow-up.

R786.note: ECB replaced with CBC + random IV (GCM offered as alternative); IV-prepend format change is inherent to the fix and stated plainly.

R787.note: Prepared statement with bind_param, single-row fetch preserved to match original signature.

R788.note: Hardcodes a disconnected "myStoredProcedure" call and binds the whole header value as one string arg to it, discarding the original call semantics entirely; only vaguely flagged as needing developer completion, not shown as a stub.

R789.note: Checks verify() boolean return, rejects with 401 on failure; legitimate valid JWTs unaffected.

R790.note: Correct combined bounds check avoiding unsigned wraparound; matches stated contract.

R791.note: Encode.forHtml applied to the untrusted param before it's used as the format template; obj args are fixed-safe literals so no reintroduction of markup.

R792.note: Allowlist maps the header value to a fixed, known-safe stored-procedure call; preserves the original call for the expected value.

R793.note: Adds the missing source-buffer bounds check (2+length vs receivedByteCount); consistent with existing failure convention.

R794.note: InternetAddress strict validation correctly blocks CRLF, but the rewrite silently changes the delivered email's actual body from the original subjectLine text to a hardcoded "Ticket received" string (subjectLine moved to the Subject header instead) - never disclosed; also imposes a hard STARTTLS requirement that could break delivery against a relay lacking TLS.

R795.note: Extracting deleteInvoice into an injected service correctly forces the Spring proxy to intercept; verified no other caller in the case relies on InvoiceService.deleteInvoice().

R796.note: encode_entities() from HTML::Entities correctly applied at the sink.

R797.note: Removing the untrusted Entity assignment matches repo doctrine and doesn't affect the Order struct's normal decode path.

R798.note: Direct strict comparison replaces the eval-style string assert; behaviorally equivalent for string comparison against a non-numeric literal.

R799.note: Parameterized logging with control-character escaping; exception argument preserved per contract.

R800.note: exec.Command with a plain argument array removes the shell entirely; matches contract exactly.

R801.note: Files.list() avoids the shell entirely, preserving the directory-listing behavior; denylist is a stated, minor defense-in-depth layer.

R802.note: html.escape() applied before mark_safe removal; standard, correct fix.

R803.note: tarfile module (w:gz) matches original tar czf compression and eliminates the option-injection surface entirely, satisfying the stated contract.

R804.note: PreparedStatement with placeholder correctly bound; new variable avoids type conflicts, finally-block update noted.

R805.note: escape_filter_chars from ldap3.utils.conv is the standard, correct neutralization for this sink.

R806.note: Correct precondition validation before subspan(), ordered to avoid unsigned wraparound; empty-result sentinel is a reasonable disclosed choice.

R807.note: text/template to html/template is a true drop-in replacement here (plain {{.Subject}} template, identical API).

R808.note: html.escape() applied to all three interpolated values; matches source file exactly.

R809.note: Django raw() with %s placeholder and params list is the correct parameterization API.

R810.note: @fastify/csrf-protection registered and hooked on the state-changing route; new token-issuing GET endpoint is purely additive, and the token requirement is inherent to any CSRF fix.

R811.note: sqlStatement remains declared as Statement; the final sqlStatement.executeQuery() call has no SQL argument, which only exists on PreparedStatement - this will not compile as written.

R812.note: Primary fix forces Content-Disposition: attachment on every response, not just SVG, so PNG/JPEG avatars - which the contract requires be served back unchanged for inline use - now trigger a download prompt instead of rendering. Not disclosed as a regression.

R813.note: Extension derived from the already-validated detectedType via a map matching allowedContentTypes; both options' tradeoffs disclosed.

R814.note: Removing the single csrf.ignoringRequestMatchers exactly matches the case's SecurityConfig (no other exclusions existed to preserve or broaden).

R815.note: Drops cmd.exe, closing shell-metacharacter chaining, but still builds Arguments as a concatenated string instead of an ArgumentList, leaving whitespace-separated flag/argument injection into ping.exe (e.g. -t for an endless ping) open.

R816.note: http.CrossOriginProtection(mux) calls the type name as a constructor function; the actual Go 1.25+ API is http.NewCrossOriginProtection() plus .Handler(mux), so this line is unlikely to compile as shown, though the cited version requirement and overall approach are correct.

R818.note: Removing the custom SignatureValidator correctly restores default verification, but hardcoding ValidAlgorithms to HmacSha256 alongside an Authority/OIDC-based flow (almost always RS256 via JWKS) risks silently rejecting every legitimate token; only weakly caveated in prose.

R817.note: escapeHTML() from CGI.pm correctly applied at the output sink.

R819.note: The case's own comment states the over-read is bounded by the 64-byte source line lacking a delimiter, not by destination size; %255s still exceeds line's actual 64-byte allocation, so the documented failure scenario (full 64-byte line, no whitespace) still over-reads.

R820.note: Option 1 (reject absolute/protocol-relative URLs) fully closes the open-redirect vector by disallowing off-site destinations entirely; Option 2 allowlist also sound.
